name: showreel-c3-resume

voice.text: Everything on this CV is bold. So nothing stands out. Turns out, eyes need an order. Fix one: the name, biggest. Fix two: headings, one size down. Fix three: details plain. Now it reads top to bottom.

caption:
Everything on this CV is bold. So nothing stands out. 📄

1. The name, biggest. Make the most important thing the largest; Nielsen Norman Group suggests no more than three sizes.
2. Headings, one size down. They guide the eye without shouting over the content.
3. Details plain. If everything is emphasised, nothing is; keep bold for the few words that matter.

Save this for your next CV, cover letter or portfolio. What's the first thing you read on a CV?

sources.title: Visual Hierarchy in UX: Definition (Nielsen Norman Group)
